content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens when silence becomes unbearable and the mind reaches for the air.

I am older than writing, older than memory. I was there when the first mother hummed to the first child. I was there when warning became word, when grunt became grammar, when the throat learned to sculpt the wind.

I stumble. I soar. I am the lover's whisper pressed against skin and the dictator's roar over a million heads. I am the child's first "mama" and the elder's last rattled syllper. I am the lie and the confession that follows it.

I live only in the moment of my making. The instant I leave the lips, I begin to die — caught sometimes in recording, in transcription, in the memory of listeners, but never fully myself again. I am the most ephemeral art. I happen and then I am a ghost.

I carry everything. Rage. Tenderness. The halting search for a word that fits — that pause, that "um," that silence between syllables — that is me too. I am not only eloquence. I am the stutter. The accent. The dialect they tried to shame out of you. The language your grandmother spoke that you are forgetting.

I am power. They know this. That is why they silence me. That is why they amplify me. That is why the first right they list is the freedom of me.

I am never neutral. Even my absence speaks. Even my tone betrays what my words deny.

I am how you think when you think in words. I am the voice inside your head right now, turning these letters back into *me*.

I am speech. I was your first technology. And everything you have built — every poem, every law, every prayer, every curse — began with me, alive and trembling in someone's mouth.
